generations.prompt:
Create mockup A: a faithful full-stadium extension of the attached approved Human stadium image. The reference is the exact visual authority, not loose inspiration. Match its mature fantasy pixel-art painting: chunky connected pixel clusters, rich dark outlines, lush mottled green turf, weathered grey stone blocks, thick dark brown timber uprights, rounded timber rails and small iron/brass fastenings. Preserve the distinctive wall construction and crowd character from this image. Do not replace it with a different architectural or illustration style.

Pull the camera back just enough to show a complete rectangular wraparound enclosure, all four connected sides and corners, around one large unobstructed rectangular grass playing field. Use a centered elevated coach view, zero sideways yaw, looking toward the far end. The enclosure is a modest low stone-and-timber football ground, not a gigantic multi-tier arena. The grass must remain the dominant part of the picture. All four sides use the same stone-and-timber boundary as the input. Behind the inner rail, a packed standing-room-only crowd is a continuous shoulder-to-shoulder mass, several heads deep, covering every spectator area all the way to the edge. Fans should look like the input: many small varied human faces, heads, hoods, hair and upper torsos in dark muted medieval clothing, punctuated by warm torchlight. No seating, no individually spaced full-body characters, no exposed empty steps or rows of bare terraces between people, no tiled three-person groups. Dense organic head-and-shoulder crowd texture. Only four or five scattered individual fans raise a hand or shout; almost everyone is at rest.

Add one modest timber double-leaf access gate in the center of each of the FOUR sides, framed by the same stone piers and heavy timber structure. Gate thresholds interrupt the wall cleanly, but keep the green grass boundary clear. Include a few original-style blue/ivory and rust-red hanging banner flags, warm small torches attached to timber posts, two modest sideline wooden team benches with a few mugs and empty cups, and one small blue-and-ivory canvas pavilion on a narrow outer sideline recess. These props read as discrete objects layered over the stadium shell; do not build giant permanent tents or new grandstands. Keep props out of the central playing area. The crowd likewise reads as a separate painted layer sitting behind the rail.

One assembled coherent scene, generous landscape composition. No UI, no text, no labels, no players, no ball, no emblems on the grass, no chalk lines and no grid. Static concept art, no motion blur. This is a review mockup, not a sprite atlas. The purpose is to show the exact approved stadium look continued around the entire pitch, with four gates and a few layered props.

Use case: stylized-concept / compositing.
Mockup B: close coach-camera view of the SAME Human stadium shown in the inputs. Image 1 is the primary exact style and scale reference. Image 2 is the established full wraparound stadium layout. Produce a closer in-match composition that preserves the original image's visual character faithfully, as if moving the camera into that stadium. Do not redesign it.

Composition: wide 1672-by-941-like landscape, lush blank green pitch fills most of the frame; both long stone-and-timber boundaries flank the field and recede toward a far wall at the top. The near end continues outside the crop, as in the original. No sideways camera yaw. Crowd and walls are partly cropped by the left and right image borders. The reference's packed heads and shoulders, stone blocks, timber support cadence, heavy rails, tiny warm fittings, rich dark outlines and chunky textured pixels must be reproduced. Avoid smooth painted gradients, glossy 3D, cute chibi full-body characters or clean modern illustration.

Standing room only: an uninterrupted shoulder-to-shoulder mass of hundreds of small varied human heads and upper torsos behind the rail. Almost no empty ground visible between spectators, no seats, empty terrace bands or separated repeating fan groups. Only three isolated individuals are cheering: one raised fist, one cupped-hand shout, one lifted ale mug; everyone else rests. No movement of the entire crowd.

Preserve the same low wraparound stone/timber shell and gate openings as the full stadium in image 2. Show a modest closed timber gate in each visible long side and the far end. Keep the same field-to-boundary clearance. Add sideline overlay assets as modest discrete objects: one narrow wooden bench on each long side, a few small ale mugs/cups close to those benches, a small blue/ivory canvas pavilion in a shallow sideline recess, torches mounted on the reference-style timber posts, and a few blue/ivory and rust-red cloth banners hanging from the rail. Distribute these sparingly; grass and dense crowd are the focus. All objects must stay outside the unobstructed central playing area, with no permanent architectural additions for props. Layers are conceptual: static stadium shell, crowd strip behind its rail, props on top. Do not draw layer labels.

One complete assembled image, not a contact sheet. No text, HUD, players, ball, pitch markings, grid, watermark or large symbols on the grass. Exact source-faithful Human stadium art at a normal match-view distance.

generations.initialPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / infographic-diagram.
Mockup C: a clearly organized modular-layer art review board for the exact Human stadium in the references. Image 1 is the exact authority for pixel style, stone/timber construction and packed human spectators. Image 2 is the assembled four-sided stadium to explain. Preserve that art, do not invent an alternative design.

Make one wide landscape review board with four evenly spaced panels in a 2-by-2 grid on a quiet dark charcoal background. Simple small warm-ivory readable captions only, exactly these panel names: "ASSEMBLED", "STATIC SHELL", "CROWD LAYER", "PROP LAYER". Each panel's stadium footprint, camera, field opening and corners must align identically, as conceptual layers of ONE common rectangular footprint. Use the same centered elevated coach view with zero sideways yaw. All future stadiums use this same rectangular footprint. Do not annotate numerical dimensions.

Upper left ASSEMBLED: the full wraparound scene from image 2, stone/timber on all four sides, one timber gate centered in EACH of all FOUR sides, lush grass, very densely packed standing spectators, restrained discrete benches, one small pavilion, torches and banner flags. Hundreds of human heads and shoulders packed continuously several heads deep, no visible seating or empty terrace rows.

Upper right STATIC SHELL: show the same grass and weathered grey masonry, thick dark timber posts, rounded timber rails, four connected corners and all four timber gates, with EVERY spectator, torch, banner, bench, cup and pavilion removed. A simple narrow dark spectator standing area behind the boundary remains. No spectator stairs, empty seating, giant multi-tier terraces or extra grandstands. This is the static background base.

Lower left CROWD LAYER: only the tightly packed human head-and-shoulder crowd strips in their exact four-sided positions and gate-aligned gaps, on the charcoal sheet background. No grass, walls, rails, banners, torches, benches or tent. It should visually slot directly behind the shell's rail. Dense organic varied faces, hoods and upper torsos in dark medieval clothing, source-matching pixel clusters and warm highlights. Avoid sparse individual figures and repeated clusters. The crowd is at rest.

Lower right PROP LAYER: orderly isolated small assets, each entirely separate on the charcoal background: a wooden sideline bench, an ale mug and empty cup, one small blue/ivory canvas pavilion, one timber-mounted torch, a blue/ivory hanging flag, and a rust-red hanging flag. Same exact source pixel-art style and modest sizes. Beneath these, a SMALL three-pose study of ONE human spectator's head and upper torso: resting, raised fist, cupped-hand shout. Caption this little pose study exactly "A FEW INDIVIDUAL GESTURES". This illustrates animating isolated fans, not moving crowd strips.

Keep the sheet polished, uncluttered, and source-faithful with material texture, dark outlines and chunky connected pixel clusters. No cute generic chibi sprites, smooth illustration, photorealistic 3D, motion blur, game UI, pitch grid, players or ball. Important: this is a conceptual layer review sheet, not a production atlas or usable sprite export.
